source.title: Language Guidance for Supervised Vision Training: An Empirical Study of Generalization
source.authors: Shruthi Gowda; Nikita Jain; Elahe Arani; Bahram Zonooz

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as motivation, but does not test whether independently trained models converge with scale or performance. Its similarity result concerns within-model cross-domain features after language guidance, not the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports increased cross-domain feature similarity in DN4IL with language guidance. This is related to representation geometry, but it does not measure similarity between independently trained models, and the guidance is deliberately introduced during training. Other reported classification, robustness, and continual-learning results do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis is cited only as motivation in Related Works. The study trains ResNet/ViT classifiers with deliberately added language supervision: ExLG uses a similarity-preserving loss toward frozen language-model embeddings, and ImLG inserts a frozen language block. It then reports accuracy, robustness, shortcut and continual-learning results. Its only similarity result (Figure 1, appendix B.1 CKA) compares cross-domain features within guided vision models against a vision-only baseline. That alignment is induced on purpose by the training objective. The study never measures convergence between independently trained models, across seeds, with scale, or for paired image-caption data.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ExLG and ImLG have complementary strengths. ExLG helps clean accuracy, low-data performance and continual-learning retention. ImLG helps more in shortcut-sensitive settings and under strong adversarial attacks. Both reduce texture bias. The Figure 1 similarity result is presented as motivation that language guidance can alter visual representation geometry.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains vision models with explicit language-similarity supervision or an inserted frozen language block; it does not reproduce a cross-model convergence measurement or scale sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Vision models trained with explicit or implicit language guidance show higher cross-domain feature similarity on DN4IL than a vision-only ResNet18. This is shown qualitatively in Figure 1 and analysed with CKA in appendix B.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary supervision from a frozen language model increases the similarity of a vision model's representations across visual domains.

record.problems: The similarity result is presented qualitatively through Figure 1, without numeric values or uncertainty in the text. The comparison concerns intentionally language-guided training and within-model cross-domain similarity, so it cannot establish spontaneous cross-model convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Classification, OOD accuracy, shortcut, texture-bias, adversarial-robustness, and continual-learning results were omitted because they do not measure representation convergence or a listed version.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep measuring alignment between independently trained models.
No measurement of vision-language alignment on paired data as both models improve. The language model is frozen and the alignment is imposed by a loss.
No comparison of networks from different initializations.
No mapping, stitching, or relative-representation interchangeability test. ImLG's trained projection into a frozen language block is a design choice, and its loss of fidelity is not evaluated.
No search for recurring features or circuits across models.
No variation of similarity metric, its settings, or inputs.
No test of plateauing or of shared-data or shared-objective explanations of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The ablations comparing Sentence Transformer, a larger language model and the CLIP text encoder (Tables 10-11) report only downstream accuracy, not representational alignment, so they bear on no version. The record's T6/cites_only classification is upheld.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No measurement of paired image-caption alignment as both vision and language models improve; no paired image-text data are used.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations for shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No systematic variation of similarity measure, settings, or input distribution to test metric or data dependence.
No test of whether alignment plateaus or is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: ExLG and ImLG language-guided vision models (reported jointly)
rows.stage_stated: supervised vision training with language guidance
rows.operation_detail: Figure 1 compares cross-domain feature similarity in DN4IL with and without language guidance.
rows.value: figure only; text states cross-domain similarity increases with language guidance
rows.note: The paper does not report separate numeric outcomes for ExLG and ImLG in the text. This is similarity across domains within vision-model representations, not alignment between independently trained models; the vision-only model is the reference.
rows.check: Linking to no version is correct. The state 'observed' refers only to the study's own claim that cross-domain similarity rises with guidance, which is shown in Figure 1 without numbers. The similarity is induced by ExLG's alignment loss or ImLG's inserted frozen block, so it cannot count as spontaneous convergence. Appendix B.1 suggests the measure is CKA, but it does not state which pairs are compared or give any values. The appendix text discusses mainly per-domain accuracy gains rather than similarity values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
